Subject: EU-South rolling IO drain & KV cache preservation — scheduled window

Hi Samantha / Acme ops team,

Quick heads up: we have a planned maintenance window for the EU-South region to perform a rolling kernel/NIC driver swap and an associated IO-eviction mitigation exercise. We’ll use a staged drain flow that preserves application-level KV caches and warm prefix caches where possible to minimize tail latencies.

Summary
- Window: 2026-10-21 00:30 — 04:30 UTC (local: 2026-10-21 01:30 — 05:30 CET)
- Impact: transient connection resets during active node drain; typical per-request latency increase 200–500ms for affected requests while active reconnect/rehydration occurs. No expected data loss — KV cache will be checkpointed to local nvme and warmed on failback.
- Canaries: initial 8-node canary (15 minutes) -> progressive 20% batch -> remaining fleet.
- Fallback: immediate rollback to current driver; traffic will be shifted to adjacent capacity region if rollback takes longer than 20 minutes for a given batch.

Action items for Acme
1) Please confirm whether you want us to run the canary during your low-traffic slice (we recommended: 00:30 UTC).
2) If you have long-lived TCP connections (keepalives > 10m), please advise — we can enable a short connection draining TTL for your routes.

Attachments: maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf (includes runbook, rollback steps), kv-persistence-playbook.md (cache checkpointing details), scheduled-window.ics (invite).

We’ll post live updates in the incident channel and send a short post-maintenance status and postmortem within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Ops — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

If those two are OK we’ll confirm and share a short list of test keys and an internal pager contact.
